meta.experiment: entry-side conditioning on entry-anchored honest cohort: 5 pre-entry features x class, R1/R2/R3 discipline, pair rules, negative filters
meta.cohort_sql:
SELECT id, symbol, direction, asset_class, opened_at, entry_price,
       intrabar_status, intrabar_pnl_pct
FROM at_signal_outcomes
WHERE intrabar_resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND intrabar_status IN ('TP_HIT','SL_HIT')
meta.bars_join: CRYPTO/MEMECOIN -> crypto_ohlcv 1h; all other classes -> stock_ohlcv 1h; pre-entry = bar_open_ms + 3600000 <= entry_ms (bar fully closed before entry; no look-ahead)
meta.dedup: per (symbol, direction, DATE(opened_at)) keep earliest opened_at (memory rule: always dedup per symbol-day; 25% dup rate raw)

features.F1_trend: last pre-entry close vs SMA50(pre-entry closes) x direction -> ALIGNED/CONTRARIAN
features.F4_vol: pstdev(last 72 1h returns) vs median of rolling sigma72 (step 4, <=400 pre-entry bars, current window excluded) -> HIGH/LOW
features.F5_session: opened_at UTC hour -> ASIA<7 / EU 7-13 / US 13-21 / OFF 21-24

discipline.R1: median-opened_at split of the slice; BOTH halves WR>=50 and PF>=1.2
discipline.R3: exact one-sided binomial P(X>=wins | n, class_baseline_wr) < 0.005
discipline.improving_flag: n>=30 and (WR lift >= 10.0pp or PF crosses 1.5)

meta.scale_guard: picks with entry_price / last_pre-entry_close outside [0.5, 2.0] excluded (entry_scale_mismatch)
meta.multiple_testing_note: 101 slices scanned; expected false positives at p<0.005 ~= 0.51; survivor p=0.0003 -> Bonferroni x101 ~= 0.03 (still <0.05 family-wise)

CRYPTO.verdict: CANDIDATE — at least one entry-condition survives R1/R2/R3; repeatability plausible but needs forward n.

best_pair_scrutiny.strategy_concentration_flag: ensemble = 35/84 = 41.7% of cell (>35% bar at STRATEGY level; R2 only checked symbol)

MEMECOIN.verdict: NULL — entry-conditioning does not materially improve selection in this cohort.

EQUITY.verdict: LIFT-BUT-FRAGILE — >=10pp WR lift exists but fails discipline (time-split/concentration/significance); not repeatable as measured.

FOREX.verdict: NEGATIVE-FILTER-ONLY — no positive selection edge, but a rejection filter removes meaningful losses.

addendum_F0_direction.note: direction (LONG/SHORT) is itself entry-time information; not in the original 5-feature spec but graded with the same R1/R2/R3 bar after the pair-scrutiny revealed SHORT dominance

crypto_short_scrutiny.strategy_concentration_flag: luxalgo_confluence = 37/76 = 48.7% of CRYPTO shorts (>35% strategy-level bar; R2 only checks symbol)

headline_findings: CRYPTO pair rule [RSI(14,1h) 50-70 AND US session entry] is the only spec-grid survivor: n=84, WR 52.4% (+18.8pp vs 33.6% baseline), PF 1.73; passes R1 (54.8%/2.36 | 50.0%/1.40), R2 (top sym RENDERUSDT 7.1%), R3 (p=3e-4; Bonferroni x101 ~ 0.03). Scrutiny: survives ensemble-strategy exclusion (57.1% WR, p=6e-4) and long-only re-test vs long-only baseline (46.4% vs 30.7%, p=4.5e-3). Spread over 14 weeks, max week 22.6%.

ADDENDUM F0: direction itself is the strongest entry-time condition. CRYPTO SHORT n=76 WR 59.2% PF 1.46 passes R1/R2/R3 (p=2.7e-6) vs LONG 30.4%/0.68 — BUT 48.7% of shorts are luxalgo_confluence (70.3% WR PF 2.12 n=37); ex-luxalgo shorts = 48.7% WR PF 0.76 (WR lift, PF<1). The honest unit is the strategy-direction cell 'luxalgo_confluence SHORT', not 'all shorts'.

EQUITY: F4_vol=LOW gives +15.7pp (62.9% WR, PF 2.48, n=35) and F4_vol=HIGH is the best negative filter (16.7% WR, captures 64.3% of class losses) — but n too small for R3 (p=0.046) and R1 fails; LIFT-BUT-FRAGILE.
FOREX: pure negative-filter story — rejecting F1 CONTRARIAN entries removes 75.7% of losses (remaining 64.3% WR PF 4.74 but n=14); consistent with forex_rsi2 memory lead; needs forward n.
MEMECOIN: NULL — no condition lifts a 28.1% WR cohort; this is a do-not-trade class, not a conditioning problem.

Net answer: entry-side conditioning CAN flip selection in CRYPTO (the only class with enough n to prove it), and the biggest single lever is direction/strategy-cell selection — corroborating the sigma-geometry conclusion that losses are selection losses, not exit-geometry losses.
